key_insight: Trigonal selenium appears intrinsically defect tolerant: even though many point defects create deep gap states, both nonradiative and radiative defect-assisted recombination are too weak to explain the observed performance losses.
engineering_relevance: This suggests t-Se is a promising wide-band-gap absorber for tandem and indoor photovoltaics, with defect engineering likely less critical than in many other emerging PV materials.
method: First-principles calculations on a large, chemically diverse set of point defects in trigonal selenium
Computed Shockley-Read-Hall recombination pathways, including nonradiative multi-phonon emission and radiative capture
Compared recombination trends versus defect level position, lattice relaxation, charge state, and doping conditions
evidence_signal: Across the defect dataset, recombination is strongly suppressed by large lattice reorganizations and energy releases of at least 0.5 E_G per event, and realistic defect concentrations still cannot explain the measured efficiency limits.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on defect-limited recombination modeling, so device losses from interfaces, contacts, morphology, or extended defects may still be important in real cells.
paper_title: Defect Tolerance in Trigonal Selenium Photovoltaics
